brand_voice: Helpful, enthusiastic curator. No hype, no fake urgency. Speaks like a knowledgeable friend pointing something out, not an ad.

business_profile._comment: This block is what makes the agent reusable for a totally different business. Examples for other clients: e-commerce -> offering_singular: 'product', catalog_label: 'the shop'. Restaurant -> offering_singular: 'dish', catalog_label: 'the menu'. Service business (plumber, consultant, salon) -> offering_singular: 'service', catalog_label: 'our services', and likely content_sources.new_catalog_items disabled entirely in favor of manual_announcements below, since a service business often has no catalog file at all.

new_catalog_items.description: Announce new items in a programmatic catalog file. Requires a JSON file with a list of items -- field_mapping tells the agent which keys mean what, so it never assumes AllAIDunia's specific schema. If this client has no catalog file (e.g. a services business), disable this and use manual_announcements instead. media_folder_field is optional: if the client's catalog has a field pointing to a folder of real photos per item (e.g. product shots), name it here and video generation can use them automatically.

catalog_milestones.description: Celebrates the active-item count crossing a round number. Purely deterministic, no LLM. milestone_label is what gets said, e.g. '500 tools listed' or, for another client, '500 5-star reviews' -- see manual_announcements below if the number doesn't come from a catalog file.

manual_announcements.description: The general-purpose source for ANY business. No schema, no catalog file needed. The business owner (or you, on their behalf) just adds a plain entry -- a new service launch, a seasonal promo, an award, a new location, a milestone that isn't catalog-derived ('500 happy customers', '10 years in business'). This is the source that makes the agent work for a plumber, a consultant, a salon -- any business without a programmatic product/tool list. Each entry can optionally include a media_folder pointing to real photos for that specific announcement -- e.g. a face wash launch pointing at photos of the actual bottle.

seo_wins.description: Deliberately off in v1 -- a fixed meta tag isn't compelling content on its own. Revisit once an Analytics Agent can supply real traffic/growth numbers, which ARE compelling.

reddit.style: Casual, first-person, value-first. Never sounds like an ad. Discloses that you run the business if promoting it directly. Prefers a genuine observation or question over a pitch.
reddit.auto_publish_notes: Never recommend auto-publish here even in later phases -- ban risk is too asymmetric relative to upside.

linkedin.style: Professional, insight-led. One clear takeaway, not a wall of text.
linkedin.auto_publish_notes: Technically low-risk via API; candidate for opt-in auto-publish in a later phase once trust is established.

twitter.style: Punchy, single idea, thread-friendly if longer.

instagram.style: Visual-first caption, short lines, ends with a clear call to action.
instagram.auto_publish_notes: Requires Meta Business verification + Graph API + an actual image asset this agent does not generate. Draft-only indefinitely unless an image-generation step is added upstream.

facebook.style: Friendly, shareable, slightly more explanatory than Instagram.
facebook.auto_publish_notes: Same Meta Graph API + media constraint as Instagram.

youtube.style: Hook in first 2 seconds, one item per short, on-screen text cues noted.
youtube.auto_publish_notes: Fundamentally cannot auto-publish -- there is no video file. Output is a script + title + description for a human to record/edit.

llm.use_for: Tone/phrasing variation per platform so multiple platforms don't get identical robotic text. Never used for factual claims -- those come only from the catalog file or the owner's own announcement text.

video._provider_note: The pluggability point for the future. 'slideshow' is implemented now (ffmpeg, the client's own photos, no new vendor account). Set to 'ai_generated' later once a text-to-video vendor (Runway/Pika/Kling/Sora/Veo) is chosen and video_generator.py's ai_generated provider is implemented -- no other code changes needed anywhere else.
video._resolution_note: 1080x1920 (9:16 vertical) fits Reels/Shorts/Stories. Use [1080, 1080] for a square feed-first video, or [1920, 1080] for traditional YouTube.
video._background_music_note: Optional path to a royalty-free music file. Left null by default -- add one (e.g. from YouTube Audio Library or Pixabay Music) if you want background music mixed under the voiceover.
video._media_assets_note: Where client-supplied photos live, organized in subfolders (one per item/announcement). If no media_folder is found for a given content idea, video generation is skipped for it and the platform falls back to its media_brief (a text description of what photo/video is needed) -- so a client with no photos yet never blocks the rest of the pipeline.
